RC-001.note: Native Screenshot transport resolves and subscribes the unique owner before requesting pixels, uses native consent without an automatic retry, verifies the returned request handle and produces no overlay on denial/cancellation/failure. Private-bus tests exercise actual production transport and controller, missing/disconnected services, cold-start/legacy response ordering, owner/sender/path fencing and invalid input. Complete native backend/permission/compositor qualification and human security review remain Required. Audit 2026-11-03 (Aoife, at ef77af6): The portal owns the native consent prompt; denied, restricted, missing/disconnected transport and cancel-at-availability all fail before any overlay, and the overlay appears only after pixels are delivered. Remaining items above are qualification, not implementation status.

RC-002.note: The portal owns native consent; explicit NotAllowed/AccessDenied errors return capture-permission-denied once. Response code 1 is user cancellation, not an inferred denial. Private-bus production tests prove no overlay, clipboard or save on denial and value-free diagnostics. Historical single-display Hyprland smoke evidence is not full qualification. Permission-settings navigation where available, physical consent and human capture-permission/security review remain Required. Audit 2026-11-03: Native consent and no prompt loop: the screenshot portal owns first-request consent and an explicit NotAllowed/AccessDenied returns capture-permission-denied once (PortalScreenshotTest::executionPreservesPrePipelineOutcomes denied row, PortalScreenshotTest::denialOffersPermissionGuidanceOnceAndNeverRepromptsOrLeavesOutput asserts one portal call, one capturePermissionDenied signal after settling, no overlay and no output). The denial now offers a 'How to allow screen capture' dialog (app/CapturePermissionHelp.cpp, wired in CaptureFeature) explaining GNOME Settings > Privacy, KDE System Settings > Privacy and 'flatpak permission-reset com.xerahs.app' for the portal store, with an Open Settings action that starts gnome-control-center privacy or systemsettings detached when found on PATH (the desktop's own app is preferred). CapturePermissionHelpTest covers both branches with injected PATH and launcher: route selection by desktop and availability, launching with the right program/arguments while the guidance stays open, a visible launch failure, manual-only guidance with no Open Settings action when no settings app exists, and a single dialog however many denials arrive. Linux has no universal settings UI for the portal permission store, so the manual steps are the documented route there.

RC-003.note: Audit 2026-11-04: RegionCaptureTest::toolkitTopologyPacksEachDisplayAtItsOwnScaleAndSurvivesReordering and toolkitTopologyRejectsInvalidScaleExtentsAndDuplicateIdentity prove pre-acquisition mapping/stable identity. RegionCaptureNativeTest::qtSnapshotUsesStableIdentityAndPerScreenMetadata and topologyChangeCancelsWithoutPublishing (add/remove/geometry/scale/rotation/identity) prove native metadata and cancellation. Native signals plus a Qt 6.4-compatible DPR poll and delivery/confirmation/publication checks prevent stale topology use. Screen depth and explicitly unavailable primaries/transfer/HDR are recorded; full per-monitor color characteristics remain unresolved, so this row stays partial. Decision 2026-11-04 (Aoife/Mike): Qt screen enumeration is the pre-acquisition authority, as in Flameshot/reference XerahS; identity hashes name/manufacturer/model/serial, each extent uses its own DPR, rotation uses orientation. Unspecified origins follow reference XerahS NormalizeCumulative (provenance in app/SOURCE-TOPOLOGY-REVIEW.md). Exact portal bitmap-size disagreement fails capture-topology-mismatch without guessing/resampling; this is the accepted degraded Qt/compositor disagreement outcome.
